title: Isolation Levels
subtitle: Understanding concurrency anomalies (Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, Phantom Reads, Write Skew) and ANSI SQL isolation guarantees.
keyTakeaways: Read Committed (default in PostgreSQL) prevents dirty reads, but allows non-repeatable reads and write skew within the same transaction.
Repeatable Read / Snapshot Isolation prevents non-repeatable reads by freezing a snapshot at transaction start, yet remains vulnerable to Write Skew.
Serializable (via SSI or 2PL) guarantees execution equivalent to a serial one-by-one schedule, eliminating all concurrency anomalies at the cost of serialization retries.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: When multiple transactions execute concurrently, subtle race conditions emerge if isolation is weak. Beyond classic Dirty Reads (reading uncommitted data) and Non-Repeatable Reads (reading a row twice and seeing different committed values), senior engineers must watch out for Lost Updates and Write Skew.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: Read Committed (default in PostgreSQL) prevents dirty reads, but allows non-repeatable reads and write skew within the same transaction.
**Problem Space & Invariants**: Repeatable Read / Snapshot Isolation prevents non-repeatable reads by freezing a snapshot at transaction start, yet remains vulnerable to Write Skew.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for Isolation Levels:
bullets: **Read Committed / Snapshot Isolation**: Provides high concurrency, zero read locks, minimal transaction abort rates. Best suited for General CRUD microservices, social feeds, and read-heavy dashboards.

**Serializable Isolation (SSI)**: Provides mathematically eliminates all concurrency anomalies; simplifies application correctness reasoning. Best suited for Core banking ledgers, auction bidding, and double-entry accounting systems.
Lost Update: Two transactions read `counter = 10`, both increment in memory, and both write `11`, losing one increment.
Phantom Read: Transaction A queries `WHERE status = 'ON_CALL'`, Transaction B inserts a new matching row and commits, changing the result set of A's range query.
Two-Phase Locking (2PL): Traditional serializable implementation using shared/exclusive and predicate/gap locks; prone to deadlocks.
Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI): Optimistic approach tracking `SIREAD` locks in memory; requires application retry loops on `40001` errors.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply Isolation Levels across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for General CRUD microservices, social feeds, and read-heavy dashboards, suited for environments requiring High concurrency, zero read locks, minimal transaction abort rates.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Core banking ledgers, auction bidding, and double-entry accounting systems, where Mathematically eliminates all concurrency anomalies; simplifies application correctness reasoning.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: PostgreSQL's default is `READ COMMITTED` (each statement sees a fresh snapshot of data committed before that statement began), whereas MySQL InnoDB's default is `REPEATABLE READ` (snapshot established at the first read in the transaction, using gap locks for locking reads). Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of Isolation Levels introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: susceptible to subtle invariants breaking via write skew or lost updates if not explicitly locked.
**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: cpu overhead tracking read dependencies and mandatory client retries on contended keys.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for Isolation Levels:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Serializable (via SSI or 2PL) guarantees execution equivalent to a serial one-by-one schedule, eliminating all concurrency anomalies at the cost of serialization retries.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Know the default isolation level of your chosen database (PostgreSQL = Read Committed, MySQL InnoDB = Repeatable Read) and be ready to explain the 'On-Call Doctors' Write Skew anomaly when asked why Repeatable Read isn't fully Serializable.
